edges.note: Monitoring a device condition (supply voltage vs safe threshold) and reacting before it violates design assumptions is the condition-monitoring tactic at power scale.
The brown-out response is typically holding reset or a controlled shutdown into the defined safe state.
Same-name pair: BIST is the standard firmware realization of the Bass Self-Test availability tactic (component-run procedures verifying its own correct operation).
Tripping open and rejecting calls to a dependency judged faulty is the ignore-faulty-behavior tactic made stateful and automatic; no circuit-breaker arch element exists yet (missing).
A recorded-acquisitions cleanup path is a C-level mechanism for the handling half of the exception-handling tactic (release exactly what was obtained on error).
Two C disciplines for single-exit resource release on error: conditional record-driven cleanup vs forward-jump to a labeled cleanup section.
Validating all parameters at component boundaries every time is the sanity-checking tactic (validity checks at interfaces) applied exhaustively.
The same boundary checking, viewed from the security side, is the validate-input tactic's check-as-received discipline.
All-or-nothing assignment via construct-then-nonthrowing-swap gives the transactions tactic's atomicity (all updates or none) at single-object scale.
Post-mortem state capture is the payload a diagnosis/maintenance channel retrieves; missing a more specific postmortem-diagnostics arch element (flight recorder/black box).
Scanning data for structural/semantic errors and repairing in place is the repair-state safety tactic applied continuously to data.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Verify Message Integrity tactic: use checksums or hash values to verify integrity of messages and files
edges.note: CRC is the named checksum mechanism of the tactic.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Condition Monitoring tactic description explicitly names computing checksums
edges.note: Checksum computation is the tactic's own example mechanism.
A persistent-redelivery messaging system needs a place to shunt messages that repeatedly fail; the dead letter channel is that load-bearing escape valve.

edges.cite: Enterprise Integration Patterns (Hohpe & Woolf), Messaging Channels chapter: Dead Letter Channel is a channel the messaging system moves undeliverable messages to
edges.note: A channel type in EIP's own taxonomy.
A timing policy for the sanity-checking tactic: run the validity check when an action requires it, scaled to consequence.
Opposite validation-placement policies: check everything at every boundary vs delay comprehensive checking until use.
Per-request key-value context (request/trace ids) attached to a thread-local stash is the in-process propagation mechanism trace correlation depends on.
Correlation ids stamped automatically on every log line are what make centrally aggregated logs searchable per request.
Routing all diagnostics through one logger that decouples producers from destinations is the in-process mechanism that lets output be redirected to a central store.
Concentrating error processing in dedicated handler components is the structural form of the exception-handling tactic (separate handling from normal flow).
Keeping irreplaceable state in a small safe core and pushing risk to expendable leaves defines the units within which errors are contained and recovered.

edges.cite: Akka documentation (supervision and the error kernel): keep important state high in the actor hierarchy, delegate risky work to child actors that can fail and be restarted
edges.note: The error kernel is articulated in terms of the supervision tree.
Progressively more drastic recovery (retry -> restart task -> restart processor) is the escalating-restart tactic; Hanmer's Escalation is its pattern-level statement.
A distinguished value object that absorbs operations on missing/invalid input keeps exceptions from arising - the exception-prevention tactic via an abstract data type.

edges.cite: Ward Cunningham, The CHECKS Pattern Language of Information Integrity: Meaningless Behavior operates over Exceptional Values, rejecting meaningless results at output
edges.note: The two CHECKS patterns are defined in terms of each other.
Checking preconditions/resources up front and reporting failure immediately is early exception detection; Nygard's stability-pattern form is missing from the arch catalog.
The Linux-kernel-style single labeled cleanup path is C's idiomatic realization of the handling/resource-release half of the exception-handling tactic.
Precondition/special-case checks at function entry detect errant conditions at the earliest point and divert flow immediately.
The guard clause is the code-shape idiom that realizes the fail-fast discipline inside a single function.
Racing staggered connection attempts over alternative paths is connection-establishment-scale failover (proactive, first-success-wins); a hedged-request tactic is missing from the arch catalog.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Availability: Heartbeat tactic - a monitored component periodically emits a message to a system monitor; missing beats mark failure
edges.note: Same-name two-realms pair: the design mechanism is the tactic's realization.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Monitor tactic description: the monitor may use heartbeat and ping/echo to observe the health of other parts
edges.note: The monitor tactic names heartbeat as one of its observation mechanisms.
The leaked error count crossing its threshold is the trigger that decides when recovery escalates to the next, more drastic level.

edges.cite: Patterns for Fault Tolerant Software (Hanmer): Riding Over Transients uses Leaky Bucket Counters to distinguish transient from persistent faults
edges.note: The two patterns are cross-referenced in the same catalog.
Abandoning in-process recovery so the unit dies and is restarted externally is the crash-only structure (only stop method is crash, only start method is recover) at process/actor scale.

edges.cite: Armstrong, Making reliable distributed systems in the presence of software errors: workers fail immediately ('let it crash') and supervisors apply restart strategies
edges.note: The philosophy presupposes the supervisor as the external recovery mechanism.
Recording errors on a dedicated diagnostic channel at the point of occurrence is what gives a central aggregation layer something faithful to collect.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Bound Execution Times tactic description names bounding iteration counts in data-dependent loops
edges.note: The bounded polling loop is the tactic's own example mechanism.
A counter/timer bound on every wait loop is the timeout tactic (detect failure to meet timing constraints) at busy-wait scale.
Tagging suspect data so later processing skips or special-cases it is the ignore-faulty-behavior tactic applied to data rather than message sources.

edges.cite: Patterns for Fault Tolerant Software (Hanmer): audits mark data they detect as erroneous but cannot repair, for later handling (Marked Data)
edges.note: Cross-referenced patterns in the same catalog.
Omitting input checks and judging validity where results are used moves the sanity check to the output/consumption interface - a placement policy for the tactic.

N independently developed implementations of one spec is exactly the diversely-designed-same-output redundancy the functional-redundancy element describes; NVP (Avizienis) is its canonical software form.

edges.cite: Avizienis, The N-Version Approach to Fault-Tolerant Software: version outputs are adjudicated by a decision algorithm/voter
edges.note: The voter is a defined part of NVP.

edges.cite: Software fault tolerance literature (Avizienis; Randell; Laprie et al. surveys) presents NVP and recovery blocks as the two principal design-diversity schemes
edges.note: Parallel-voted diversity vs sequential acceptance-tested diversity.
An error-accumulating object returned across a boundary is a handling mechanism in the tactic's stated range (return codes to exception classes), suited to expected validation errors.

edges.cite: Fowler, P of EAA catalog 'Notification': an object collecting errors from the domain layer, passed back across the service-layer boundary instead of throwing
edges.note: Fowler describes Notification at the layer boundary.
Fencing a faulty element's outputs and routing no work to it is the ignore-faulty-behavior tactic plus containment of its error propagation.
The two-track workflow is a filter chain at function-composition scale: each step transforms and passes along, with failure switching tracks; honest altitude caveat - in-code analog of the style.

edges.cite: Wlaschin, Railway Oriented Programming (fsharpforfunandprofit): composing functions over a two-track success/failure Result type
edges.note: ROP is defined as composition over result types.
Diversely implemented alternates for the same spec, engaged sequentially behind an acceptance test - the standby form of design-diversity redundancy.

edges.cite: Randell, System Structure for Software Fault Tolerance (1975): on acceptance-test failure, state is restored to the recovery point before the alternate runs
edges.note: Rollback to the recovery point is a defined step of the scheme.
Crash-only structure depends on cheap, reliable reinitialization: recovery IS restart, so the restart mechanism is load-bearing.
Supervisor restart strategies presuppose units that can be cleanly reinitialized; restartability is the mechanism the tree's recovery model rests on.
A sum type making failure part of the signature is the typed evolution of the tactic's return-code end of the handling-mechanism range.
Capping retries as a fraction of primary load is admission control applied to the retry stream, protecting the service from retry storms.

edges.cite: Site Reliability Engineering (Google), Handling Overload: per-client retry budgets (e.g. retries at most 10% of requests) bound the retry tactic's added load
edges.note: The budget is a stated guard on retrying.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Retry tactic (bounded reattempts on transient faults); AWS Builders' Library 'Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter' gives backoff+jitter as the retry discipline
edges.note: Mission calibration pair: the design element is the tactic's implementation-level realization.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Exception Handling tactic: handling mechanisms range from function return codes to exception classes
edges.note: Return codes are named in the tactic's own description.
Deliberately not reacting to momentary self-clearing errors is the ignore-faulty-behavior tactic restricted to transients.

Advancing to a new consistent state ahead of the error point repairs the erroneous state and continues - the forward-recovery form of the repair-state tactic; no roll-forward tactic exists in the arch catalog (missing).

edges.cite: Patterns for Fault Tolerant Software (Hanmer), error-recovery patterns: Roll-Forward and Rollback presented as the two recovery directions
edges.note: Forward vs backward recovery from the same catalog.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Rollback tactic: revert to a previously saved known-good state (checkpoint) and resume
edges.note: Same-name two-realms pair: identical mechanism at tactic altitude.
The monitoring channel's fault response is driving the actuation channel into the predefined safe state; the pattern depends on that state being defined and reachable.
The safety executive's coordinated shutdown/fail-safe logic presupposes engineered safe states to steer the system into.
Assert/abort at the failure point for unhandleable errors is the abort tactic (terminate before damage) applied at API scale.
The parameter fence is a known in-band pattern placed after parameters and checked for overwrite - a sentinel-value application the tactic depends on.
setjmp/longjmp is C's canonical raise-and-catch mechanism, sitting mid-range in the tactic's return-codes-to-exception-classes spectrum.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Removal from Service tactic: temporarily take a component out of service and reset it to scrub latent faults (memory leaks, fragmentation) - the mechanism named software rejuvenation (Huang et al. 1995)
edges.note: The tactic describes exactly proactive rejuvenation.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Exception Handling tactic names function return codes among handling mechanisms
edges.note: In-band failure values (NULL, -1, EOF) are the return-code mechanism.
A special return value is a sentinel reserved specifically for failure signalling in a function's return domain.
Scanning the painted pattern to measure worst-case stack depth validates a design assumption (stack sizing) at runtime - condition monitoring of a resource margin.
Filling stacks with a known pattern and checking it later is the poison-pattern technique specialized to stack usage measurement.

edges.cite: Erlang/OTP Design Principles: supervision trees are built from supervisor behaviours that monitor children and apply declared restart strategies
edges.note: Same-name pair: the supervisor component is the node the tree structure is made of.
A component whose only job is watching worker health and triggering recovery is the monitor tactic with an attached restart policy.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Timeout tactic: raise an exception when a component fails to meet its timing constraint
edges.note: Same-name two-realms pair: bounding every blocking wait is the tactic's realization.

edges.cite: Nygard, Release It!: the Timeouts and Circuit Breaker stability patterns are presented as complementary - timeouts detect the slow failure, the breaker stops repeating it
edges.note: Cross-referenced stability patterns.

edges.cite: Saltzer & Schroeder, The Protection of Information in Computer Systems (1975): access control lists as an implementation of the access matrix for authorization decisions
edges.note: ACL is a canonical authorization mechanism.

edges.cite: Saltzer & Schroeder (1975): ACLs (per-object columns) and capability lists (per-subject rows) as the two decompositions of the access matrix
edges.note: Classic duality.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Validate Input tactic (filtering/cleansing input as received); OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet names allowlist validation as the primary strategy
edges.note: The allowlist is the tactic's strongest form.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Audit tactic: keep a record of user and system actions so an attacker's actions can be traced
edges.note: The append-only audit log is the tactic's mechanism.
AE/AEAD is the modern mechanism deploying the encrypt-data tactic for data in motion and at rest.
The authentication half of AE guarantees ciphertext integrity - the tactic realized inside the encryption construction.

edges.cite: RFC 8446 (TLS 1.3): all cipher suites are AEAD-based - the secure channel's record protection is authenticated encryption
edges.note: The connector's confidentiality+integrity rests on AE.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Validate Input tactic description explicitly includes canonicalization alongside filtering and cleansing
edges.note: Canonicalization is named inside the tactic.

edges.cite: Saltzer & Schroeder (1975): capabilities as an authorization mechanism - possession of the unforgeable token is the access right
edges.note: Canonical authorization model.

edges.cite: Yoder & Barcalow, Architectural Patterns for Enabling Application Security (1997): Check Point concentrates authentication decisions in one configurable component
edges.note: Named in the pattern's intent.

edges.cite: Yoder & Barcalow (1997): Check Point also concentrates authorization and violation-response decisions
edges.note: Same pattern, second tactic.
A single configurable component making all security decisions is the application-internal precursor of the externalized PDP/PEP structure.
Token/MAC verification underlying authentication is only sound if comparison leaks nothing via timing; no side-channel-resistance tactic exists in the arch catalog (missing).

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Verify Message Integrity tactic names hash values as the integrity mechanism
edges.note: Hash digests are the tactic's stated mechanism.

edges.cite: Nakamoto, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System (2008): blocks chained by hashes, transactions in Merkle trees - the ledger's tamper-evidence is the hash function
edges.note: Load-bearing primitive of the style.
Key, IV and nonce generation for any deployed encryption depends on computationally unpredictable randomness.
Copying mutable inputs/outputs closes the aliasing hole in encapsulation, making the interface the only way to affect internals - the encapsulate tactic enforced against aliases.
The homogeneous form (two identical channels) is the replication pattern at channel scale; the heterogeneous form shades into functional redundancy.
The comparison/switchover logic between the two channels is the comparison safety tactic (detect unsafe states by output divergence).
An authorization-presentation policy: all operations visible, unauthorized attempts rejected with explicit errors at use time.

edges.cite: Yoder & Barcalow (1997) present Full View With Errors and Limited View as the two alternative UI authorization policies
edges.note: Explicit alternatives in the source catalog.
An MMU-enforced inaccessible band adjacent to a stack/allocation detects overrun of neighboring memory - the fence tactic realized in hardware traps instead of pattern checks.
Trap-on-touch page vs checked secret value: two mechanisms detecting overruns toward adjacent/control data.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Validate Input tactic includes cleansing/sanitizing input; OWASP XSS Prevention names sanitization of untrusted markup
edges.note: Sanitization is the tactic's named cleansing form.
Presenting only permitted operations enforces authorization by construction at the UI.
Poison patterns turn latent stale-memory and use-after-free faults into detectable conditions close to their cause.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Verify Message Integrity tactic (checksums/hashes); a MAC is the keyed form authenticating integrity and origin
edges.note: Keyed integrity mechanism of the tactic.
A valid MAC authenticates the message's origin as a key holder - actor authentication at message granularity.

edges.cite: Bellare & Namprempre, Authenticated Encryption: generic composition of an encryption scheme with a MAC (encrypt-then-MAC)
edges.note: AE is built from cipher plus MAC.
Challenge nonces make authentication exchanges replay-proof; no replay-resistance/freshness tactic exists in the arch catalog (missing).

edges.cite: RFC 5116 (An Interface and Algorithms for Authenticated Encryption): the AEAD interface requires a nonce, unique per key
edges.note: Nonce is a defined AEAD input.
Verifying the stored pair still complement each other on every read is continuous integrity monitoring of critical data.
Inverse-pair verification vs polynomial checksum: two RAM/data corruption detection mechanisms with different cost/coverage.
OWASP groups it with input-handling injection defenses; strictly it removes the parse-as-code channel rather than validating - an injection-prevention tactic is missing from the arch catalog.
NULL-initialize/NULL-on-free plus check-before-use keeps wild-pointer faults from arising - the exception-prevention tactic in C.
Holding elevated privilege only across the exact operations that need it minimizes the window an attack can exploit - temporal least privilege.
Temporal and structural forms of least privilege are typically deployed together.

edges.cite: Provos, Friedl & Honeyman, Preventing Privilege Escalation (2003): defines privilege separation as the small privileged monitor plus unprivileged workers - the structure both entries describe
edges.note: Same-name two-realms pair.
Verifying that execution checkpoints occur in the required order and time monitors a design assumption (control flow) at run time.

edges.cite: AUTOSAR Watchdog Manager (WdgM) specification: alive, deadline and logical (program-flow) supervision results drive the hardware watchdog
edges.note: Sequence monitoring is specified as a watchdog-manager function.
The channel's added integrity checks (CRCs, range checks, monitoring points) are the condition-monitoring tactic embedded along one data path.

edges.cite: Douglass (Design Patterns for Embedded Systems in C / Real-Time Design Patterns): Protected Single Channel and Dual Channel presented as alternative safety channel structures by risk level
edges.note: Alternatives in the source catalog.

edges.cite: Anderson, Computer Security Technology Planning Study (1972): the reference monitor mediates every access by subjects to objects against the authorization database
edges.note: The defining authorization-enforcement concept.
PDP/PEP is the distributed, externalized form of the reference monitor function (mediation of every access against policy).

edges.cite: Ferraiolo & Kuhn, Role-Based Access Controls (1992) / NIST RBAC model: permissions granted to roles, acquired by membership - an authorization mechanism
edges.note: Named access-control model realizing the tactic.
Role-indirected grants vs per-object subject lists: alternative authorization models.

edges.cite: Morris & Thompson, Password Security: A Case History (1979): salted one-way hashing as the password-store mechanism underlying password authentication
edges.note: The tactic's password form depends on this storage discipline.
Built from a (deliberately slow/iterated) one-way hash plus per-entry salt.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Sanity Checking tactic: check validity/reasonableness of a component's outputs or state, typically at interfaces
edges.note: Same-name two-realms pair: the plausibility monitor is the tactic's mechanism.
Wrapping the differing security mechanisms of underlying platforms behind one application-internal service factors their similarity into a single abstract service.
A dedicated layer in the application's stack, per the pattern's own name and structure (Yoder & Barcalow).

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Verify Message Integrity tactic explicitly covers verifying integrity of resource and deployment files via hashes
edges.note: Image verification is the tactic applied to boot/deployment artifacts.
The boot-stage architecture's 'select/validate the application image' step is load-borne by cryptographic image verification.
A TEE's trust chain roots in verified boot: the isolated partition's firmware must itself be authenticated at boot.
Erasing secrets immediately after last use shrinks the data reachable through a memory-disclosure attack - exposure limited in time.
Carrying the authenticated identity across a sequence of actions is the mechanism that amortizes authentication over a session instead of per request.

edges.cite: Yoder & Barcalow (1997): the Session pattern holds the security context that Check Point and Roles consult
edges.note: Cross-referenced patterns in the same paper.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Limit Access tactic: restrict access by limiting the number of access points - the pattern is exactly one guarded entry point
edges.note: The tactic's own wording names the mechanism.

edges.cite: Yoder & Barcalow (1997): Single Access Point performs its identity/validity checks at a Check Point
edges.note: The two patterns are defined together.
Self-validating data types that check every set/get are the abstract-data-type form of exception prevention named by the tactic.
A secret guard value between buffers and control data, verified before return, is the known-pattern fence tactic guarding the return address.
The verified per-session token authenticates the request as originating from the application's own UI in the legitimate session; a request-forgery-defense tactic is missing from the arch catalog.
A per-session/per-request unpredictable value whose freshness defeats forged/replayed requests - a nonce specialized to CSRF defense.

edges.cite: perlsec (Perl security documentation): taint mode forbids using externally derived data in sensitive operations until it is untainted via explicit validation
edges.note: The runtime enforces the validate-input tactic.
Same-name two-realms pair: the kicked timer is the mechanism at the core of the system-level watchdog supervision structure.

edges.cite: Software Architecture in Practice (Bass et al.), Heartbeat tactic description: the monitored component periodically emits a message to, or resets a watchdog timer in, the system monitor
edges.note: The tactic names the watchdog timer as one of its two mechanisms.

notes: All 90 g8 elements (error-handling + robustness-security) bridged; unbridged list empty. 109 cross-realm realizes/enables edges, 35 supplementary implements/specializes/composes-with/alternative-to edges. Sourced edges lean on Bass tactic descriptions that name the mechanism (checksums, return codes, canonicalization, watchdog timer, access points, loop bounds, rejuvenation), EIP, Hanmer, Yoder-Barcalow, Cunningham CHECKS, Randell/Avizienis, Saltzer-Schroeder, Anderson, Provos, OTP/Armstrong, Nygard, Google SRE, RFCs 8446/5116, Nakamoto, perlsec. MISSING arch bridge targets found (demand-driven growth candidates): (1) circuit breaker / Nygard stability pattern set (fail fast, handshaking) at system level; (2) hedged-request / racing-redundant-requests tactic (needed for happy-eyeballs); (3) replay-resistance / freshness tactic (nonce, synchronizer token); (4) injection-prevention tactic distinct from validate-input (parameterized query); (5) side-channel-resistance tactic (constant-time comparison); (6) postmortem-diagnostics element (black box / flight recorder) for core-dump; (7) roll-forward / forward-error-recovery tactic; (8) plain restart-as-recovery tactic below escalating-restart; (9) fail-to-safe-state safety tactic (safe-state currently bridged via monitor-actuator and safety-executive).
